resources.string: Enter a time from 1 second to 3 days.
Shows recorded attempts only. Traffic history is normally kept for up to 3 days.
No recorded attempts in this time window.
No attempts from visible apps in this time window. Check Hidden apps or extend the time window.
Couldn’t read recent traffic. Tap here to retry.
Tap the crossed-out eye to show an app again. Hiding only filters this view; logging and protection stay unchanged.
No apps hidden. Tap the eye beside an app icon to hide its traffic.
Individual-attempt recording is off. Existing recorded attempts can still appear below.
Your rules disable detailed traffic recording. Enable “feature allow_logging” in Rules, then turn recording on here. The normal rule delay applies.
Detailed traffic is hidden while your rules disallow logging.
Hide an app’s traffic from Recent traffic only
Hidden apps: restore traffic to Recent traffic
Record individual network attempts on this device? This uses the existing traffic log and does not change which connections are allowed.
DomainGuard is off. New attempts are recorded only while traffic passes through its VPN.

Each row is a separate recorded network attempt, including repeats. Newest first follows new traffic while you are at the top; scrolling keeps your place. The time window moves with the clock.

The eye beside an app hides all traffic for its network identity from this view. Hidden apps lets you show it again. Apps sharing that identity are hidden together.

The check or X shows whether that attempt was allowed or blocked at the time. Tap a domain for Allow, Block or Copy. Where a network identity belongs to several apps, choose the app before adding a rule.

Only traffic observed and recorded by DomainGuard appears here. An IP address is shown when its domain is unknown. This can reveal activity from helper apps, but cannot establish which app triggered it.
